subtasks.title: [runner] 복잡한 Jenkinsfile 실행 지원 범위 검증 및 Job/Runner 보완
subtasks.description: 복잡한 Jenkinsfile 시나리오를 기준으로 Job 생성부터 Runner 실행까지 현재 지원 범위를 검증하고, 필요한 기능 보완 포인트를 도출한다.
subtasks.details:
[source: jgitkins-server, original subtask: 1.16]
이 작업은 단순 테스트가 아니라 향후 Job 생성 및 Runner 실행 기능 확장을 위한 신규기능 성격의 검증 과제다. 우선 대표적인 복잡한 Jenkinsfile 시나리오를 선정한다. 예: scripted pipeline, declarative pipeline, parallel stage, matrix/conditional, shared library 의존, shell/script step 다수, credential 사용, agent/docker 지정, 아티팩트/워크스페이스 활용 등. 각 시나리오별로 현재 서버가 push 이후 Job 을 어떻게 생성하는지, 어떤 payload 로 Runner 에 전달하는지, Runner 가 어떤 runtime/plugin/script 제약으로 실패하는지 확인한다. 검토 및 구현 범위는 다음을 포함한다. 1) 복잡한 Jenkinsfile 샘플 세트 정의. 2) Job 생성 입력 모델과 Jenkinsfile 선택/해석 규칙이 복잡한 스크립트 구조를 수용하는지 점검. 3) Runner 측 실행 환경, plugin, 이미지, credential, filesystem/workspace 요구사항 정리. 4) 성공/실패/skip/timeout 케이스별 상태 반영과 로그 수집 전략 확인. 5) 실제 검증 결과를 바탕으로 서버/runner 어느 쪽에 기능 보완이 필요한지 후속 Task 로 분리한다. 산출물은 지원 가능 시나리오, 실패 시나리오, 즉시 보완 항목, 후속 개발 항목 목록이다.

subtasks.title: [web, server] Develop File Content Viewer UI Component with WYSIWYG
subtasks.description: Create a frontend UI component to display file content, integrating a WYSIWYG editor for rendering various file types (e.g., Markdown, code, plain text).
subtasks.details:
[source: jgitkins-server, original subtask: 1.19]
Implement a component (e.g., `FileContentViewer`) that accepts raw file content and its type (derived from file extension).
1.  For Markdown files (`.md`, `.markdown`), integrate a Markdown renderer library (e.g., `react-markdown`, `marked.js`) to display rendered HTML.
2.  For code files (e.g., `.java`, `.js`, `.py`, `.xml`), integrate a code highlighter/editor (e.g., Monaco Editor, CodeMirror, Prism.js) to display syntax-highlighted code.
3.  For plain text files, display the content directly.
4.  For unknown or binary files, display a message indicating content cannot be rendered directly.

The component should act as a viewer (read-only) as per the PRD's '읽을 수 있는 기능을 제공한다' (provides the ability to read).

subtasks.title: [server, runner] Feature Plugin Management
subtasks.description: Add a first-class plugin management workflow so each runner profile can declare the Jenkins plugins required for a pipeline, persist those definitions in the CLI config, and ensure the Docker executor mounts the resolved bundle before calling the server.
subtasks.details:
[source: jgitkins-runner, original subtask: 1.2]
- Teach the CLI config loader to read/write a `plugins` section in `~/.jgitkins-runner/config.yml`, keep named bundles per profile, and expose Picocli flags that let `run` reference a specific `plugins.yaml` manifest.
- Introduce a parser (e.g., `PluginBundleLoader` under `src/main/java/io/jgitkins/runner/infrastructure/plugins`) that reads the YAML, downloads/cache `.jpi` files, and mirrors Jenkinsfile Runner’s expected directory layout before execution.
- Extend `JobExecuteRequest` (`src/main/java/io/jgitkins/runner/presentation/api/dto/JobExecuteRequest.java`) and related DTO/command objects so `/pipelines/run` can accept an optional plugin bundle identifier or manifest path; default to the active profile’s bundle.
- Update `DockerRunnerAdapter.run` (`src/main/java/io/jgitkins/runner/infrastructure/adapter/DockerRunnerAdapter.java`) so the `Bind` list includes both the workspace and the resolved plugin volume (mount to `/usr/share/jenkins/ref/plugins` or configurable `runner.plugins.mountPath`).
- Provide CLI subcommands such as `plugins list`, `plugins sync`, and `plugins use` to inspect/update bundles, persisting changes back to the YAML config alongside existing registration data.
- Document plugin workflow in `README.md`, including how to author `plugins.yaml`, where bundles are cached, and how to override bundles per `run` invocation.
Pseudo:
```
PluginBundle bundle = pluginBundleLoader.load(activeProfile);
Bind plugins = new Bind(bundle.getPath(), new Volume(config.getPluginsMountPath()));
CreateContainerResponse container = dockerClient.createContainerCmd(image)
    .withBinds(workspaceBind, plugins)
    .exec();
```

subtasks.title: [bounded-context port 분리][refactor][server] collaboration persistence port relocation
subtasks.description: collaboration persistence contract의 소유권을 정리한다. domain 모델을 저장·수정·로딩하는 OrganizePersistencePort는 OrganizeRepository로 이름을 변경하고 collaboration.domain.repository로 이동한다. OrganizeQueryPort는 collaboration.application.port.out에 유지하는 좁은 read-only 조회 계약으로, 현재 호출부에 필요한 findByName을 추가한다. Phase 1 correctness 완료 이후 진행.
subtasks.details: 기준 spec: ~/.gstack/plans/jgitkins-collaboration-persistence-port-relocation-spec-20260818.md. 구현 기준: 1) OrganizePersistencePort와 OrganizeQueryPort의 실제 입력·반환 타입과 production/test 호출부를 inventory한다. caller에는 identity.access.application.support.UsernameAllocator, identity.access.application.validate.ActivationValidator, repository.application.support.RepositoryLookupService, shared.application.support.RepositoryNamespaceResolver와 대응 테스트를 포함한다. 2) 현재 OrganizePersistencePort는 full aggregate persistence contract이므로 OrganizeRepository로 이름을 변경하고 collaboration.domain.repository에 둔다. 3) OrganizeQueryPort는 collaboration.application.port.out에 유지하며 findById와 findByName만 제공하는 read-only application output port로 둔다. 현재 호환성을 위해 Organize를 반환할 수 있으나 save/update/delete는 포함하지 않는다. 4) OrganizeService와 OrganizeValidator는 OrganizeRepository를 주입받도록 변경하고 validator의 unused OrganizeQueryPort import를 제거한다. 5) 현재 패키지 collaboration.infrastructure.adapter.persistence의 OrganizePersistenceAdapter를 유지하며 adapter package를 이동하지 않고, 이 adapter가 OrganizeRepository와 OrganizeQueryPort를 구현하도록 wiring을 수정한다. MyBatis generated ID·예외 동작도 유지한다. 6) OrganizePersistencePort.java를 삭제하고 production/test의 old declaration/import/reference를 모두 제거한다. 7) identity.access, repository, shared가 full OrganizeRepository를 직접 참조하지 않도록 필요한 호출부만 OrganizeQueryPort로 변경한다. username allocation, activation validation, repository lookup, namespace resolution behavior를 유지한다. 8) OrganizeServiceTest는 OrganizeRepository mock으로, UsernameAllocatorTest와 ActivationValidatorTest는 OrganizeQueryPort mock으로 갱신하고, RepositoryLoadServiceTest의 stale OrganizePersistencePort import를 제거한다. RepositoryLookupService와 RepositoryNamespaceResolver에 전용 테스트가 없으면 각각의 organization lookup behavior를 검증하는 focused test를 추가한다. Architecture tests는 OrganizeRepository의 6개 method, OrganizeQueryPort의 2개 read-only method, adapter의 두 interface 구현과 component/mapper wiring 보존을 검증한다. 9) collaboration.presentation의 adapter.in 이동은 후속 task 2.48에서 수행하며 이 task에는 포함하지 않는다. 제외: API/DB schema 변경, identity.access 전체 migration, repository 전체 migration, membership lifecycle, outbox, 전체 presentation package 이동, OrganizeQueryRepository 및 OrganizationNamespaceQuery 신설.

# Task 2.63 — Standalone Implementation Specification

> Canonical plan: `/Users/hrk/.gstack/plans/jgitkins-task-2.63-identity-activation-actor-injection-20250825.md`

## Implementer contract

Use this document alone. Exact FQCNs, signatures, callers, selectors, commands, result paths, validators, ownership, compatibility, and rollback are binding.

# Task 2.63 — Explicit requester for identity activation

> Status: DRAFT — fresh CEO HOLD-SCOPE review required before spec or implementation
> Repository: `/Users/hrk/task/sources/opensources/jgitkins`
> Taskmaster: `2.63`
> Dependency: none

## Goal and ownership boundary

Move current-user derivation for signup activation to the identity inbound adapter. `SignupController` extracts the transport principal, the identity-owned resolver converts it to a numeric requester ID, and the application use case receives that ID explicitly. `UserProfileService` stops reading `CurrentUserPort` for activation only. `CurrentUserPort` remains in its existing callers: `InProcessUserIdentityAdapter`, `RepositoryActorAclAdapter`, `ActiveAccountPolicyAdapter`, and `CurrentUserSecurityAdapter`.

## Exact resolver contract

```text
FQCN: io.jgitkins.server.identity.access.adapter.in.support.RequesterUserIdResolver
bean: @Component("identityRequesterUserIdResolver")
signature: Optional<Long> resolve(String principalName)
```

Input semantics:

```text
null, empty, ASCII space/tab/newline/carriage-return-only -> Optional.empty()
[0-9]+ ASCII decimal digits, with or without leading zero, whose parsed value is greater than zero -> Optional.of(parsed ID)
any all-zero decimal string ("0", "00", "000", or any length), plus/minus, negative, non-ASCII digit, overflow, surrounding whitespace, nonnumeric -> ApplicationException(UNAUTHENTICATED, "Authentication required")
```

`0` is malformed. No tri-state result and no compatibility overload. The resolver fixture has no repository/application collaborators; resolver tests assert zero collaborator calls by construction. Controller malformed/anonymous tests assert no successful resolver result and zero `SignupUseCase`/repository interactions. Service authorization-failure tests assert no repository access after denial.

## Exact inbound extraction and use-case contract

The controller method becomes:

```text
SignupController#activate(UserUsernameUpdateRequest request, java.security.Principal principal)
```

Exact extraction:

```java
String principalName = principal == null ? null : principal.getName();
Long requesterUserId = requesterUserIdResolver.resolve(principalName)
        .orElseThrow(() -> new UnauthenticatedException("Authentication required"));
signupUseCase.activate(requesterUserId, request.username());
```

The controller uses an explicit constructor (no Lombok constructor annotation for this dependency), with the qualifier on the constructor parameter:

```java
SignupController(SignupUseCase signupUseCase,
                 @Qualifier("identityRequesterUserIdResolver") RequesterUserIdResolver requesterUserIdResolver)
```

The wiring test must assert the injected controller field/reference is an instance of the identity-owned resolver, not only that both bean names exist.

The collaboration resolver retains its current default bean name `requesterUserIdResolver`; identity and collaboration resolver beans are distinct and are not reused across bounded contexts. `UserProfileService#activate(Long requesterUserId, String username)` uses the explicit ID directly and has no `CurrentUserPort` field or call.

## Compatibility contract

Route/body remain `POST /api/signup/activate` with `UserUsernameUpdateRequest`. Preserve exact outcomes:

```text
validActivationReturnsNullableSuccessEnvelope -> 200, existing nullable data/error envelope
missingUsernameReturnsPresentationContract -> existing presentation validation status/code/message/source/envelope
invalidPatternUsernameReturnsPresentationContract -> existing presentation validation status/code/message/source/envelope
unauthenticatedReturnsApplicationContract -> 401 AUTH-001 "Authentication required", source application
missingUserReturnsApplicationContract -> 404 USER-404
duplicateUsernameReturnsApplicationContract -> 409 USER-409-USERNAME
namespaceCollisionReturnsApplicationContract -> 409 ORG-409
ownedRepositoryPreventsRenameWithApplicationContract -> 422 UNPROCESSABLE
alreadyActivatedReturnsDomainContract -> 409 USER-409-ACTIVATED
```

The two presentation methods remain in scope. No route, request body, status, code, message, source, envelope, schema, JWT, or wire change.

## Exact retained CurrentUserPort caller matrix

These callers are explicitly outside Task 2.63 activation migration and remain unchanged. Their retained disposition is `RETAINED_BASELINE`; they must not be converted to the identity requester resolver.

| FQCN | exact source path | classification | disposition |
|---|---|---|---|
| `io.jgitkins.server.collaboration.adapter.out.acl.InProcessUserIdentityAdapter` | `app-server/src/main/java/io/jgitkins/server/collaboration/adapter/out/acl/InProcessUserIdentityAdapter.java` | collaboration outbound ACL adapter; retained CurrentUserPort caller | `RETAINED_BASELINE / OUT_OF_SCOPE` |
| `io.jgitkins.server.repository.adapter.out.acl.RepositoryActorAclAdapter` | `app-server/src/main/java/io/jgitkins/server/repository/adapter/out/acl/RepositoryActorAclAdapter.java` | repository outbound ACL adapter; retained CurrentUserPort caller | `RETAINED_BASELINE / OUT_OF_SCOPE` |
| `io.jgitkins.server.identity.access.adapter.out.policy.ActiveAccountPolicyAdapter` | `app-server/src/main/java/io/jgitkins/server/identity/access/adapter/out/policy/ActiveAccountPolicyAdapter.java` | identity policy adapter; retained CurrentUserPort caller | `RETAINED_BASELINE / OUT_OF_SCOPE` |
| `io.jgitkins.server.identity.access.adapter.out.security.CurrentUserSecurityAdapter` | `app-server/src/main/java/io/jgitkins/server/identity/access/adapter/out/security/CurrentUserSecurityAdapter.java` | security adaptation adapter; retained CurrentUserPort caller | `RETAINED_BASELINE / OUT_OF_SCOPE` |

The only CurrentUserPort removal is from `UserProfileService` activation. Any diff touching these four paths is a scope violation and must fail review.

## Implemented 2026-08-27

`SignupController` now extracts the transport principal, the identity-owned resolver converts it to a
numeric id, and `UserProfileService#activate(Long requesterUserId, String username)` receives it
explicitly. `UserProfileService` no longer has a `CurrentUserPort` field. The port itself is untouched
and still serves `InProcessUserIdentityAdapter`, `RepositoryActorAclAdapter`,
`ActiveAccountPolicyAdapter` and `CurrentUserSecurityAdapter` — this task narrowed one caller, it did not
retire the port.

### Resolver semantics, and why absent and malformed are separate outcomes

| Input | Outcome |
| --- | --- |
| `null`, `""`, ASCII space/tab/CR/LF only | `Optional.empty()` — no principal was presented |
| `[0-9]+` parsing to a value greater than zero, leading zeros allowed | `Optional.of(parsed)` |
| `"0"`, `"00"`, any all-zero string, `+`/`-` signs, surrounding whitespace, non-ASCII digits, overflow, non-numeric | `ApplicationException(UNAUTHENTICATED, "Authentication required")` |

Collapsing malformed into `empty()` would let a corrupted credential take the same path as an anonymous
request. For an endpoint that mutates the caller's own account, that means a broken token is reported as
"please log in" and quietly retried rather than investigated. The client sees the same 401 either way —
the distinction is for the server and its log, which is why the two branches carry the same message.

`"0"` is malformed rather than absent because no user has id zero: a subject of `"0"` is a leaked
placeholder or a truncated value, and treating it as valid would attempt an activation against a row that
cannot exist.

The ASCII digit range is explicit rather than `Character.isDigit`. `Long.parseLong("५")` returns `5` —
the test records that fact, because it is the reason the looser check is not enough. An id whose value
depends on the script it was written in is not an id.

### The two resolvers are deliberately different, and that is what the wiring test protects

Collaboration's resolver of the same simple name uses `Long.valueOf` and swallows every failure into
`empty()`. Identity's throws. Wired to the wrong bean, a malformed principal would resolve to `empty()`
and surface as **the same 401 the client already sees** — so no HTTP-level test could detect the swap.
`IdentityRequesterResolverWiringTest` therefore reflects the field the controller actually holds, and its
second test asserts the two resolvers genuinely disagree, so the qualifier cannot quietly become
cosmetic.

`SignupController` uses an explicit constructor rather than `@RequiredArgsConstructor`, because the
qualifier has to sit on the constructor parameter and Lombok's generated constructor cannot carry it.

### Compatibility, checked rather than asserted

The nine existing `SignupActivationHttpCompatibilityTest` cases pass unchanged, now with a valid
principal on every request so the responses being compared are the ones a real authenticated caller gets.
One case was added: an anonymous request must keep the `AUTH-001` / `source: application` envelope it had
when the service raised the rejection. That is the whole compatibility claim of moving the check to the
adapter, and without it the move would be unverified.

### Negative control

Reverting the identity resolver to collaboration's lax semantics fails **20 assertions across three
tests**: 18 of the 26 resolver cases, the wiring test's disagreement assertion, and — the one that
matters most — `SignupControllerTest#activate_rejectsMalformedRequesterWithoutUseCaseInteraction`, where a
malformed principal turns a 401 into a **200**. A malformed credential would have activated an account.

### Guard kept in the service as well as the adapter

`UserProfileService#activate` rejects a null `requesterUserId` even though the adapter is its only
current caller. A use case that trusts its arguments is one refactor away from activating an arbitrary
account, and the check costs a branch.

609 tests, 0 failures, 1 skipped; `:app-server:bootJar` succeeds.

# Task 2.64 — Standalone Implementation Specification

> Canonical plan: `/Users/hrk/.gstack/plans/jgitkins-task-2.64-repository-mutation-actor-injection-20250825.md`
> Implementation status: BLOCKED until Task 2.63 gate and declared evidence pass.
> Review boundary: no execution is implied.

## Implementer contract

Use this document alone. Exact FQCNs, signatures, callers, selectors, commands, result paths, validators, ownership, compatibility, rollback, and technology boundaries are binding.

## Canonical executable contract

# Task 2.64 — Repository mutation actor injection

> Status: DRAFT — fresh CEO HOLD-SCOPE review required before spec or implementation
> Repository: `/Users/hrk/task/sources/opensources/jgitkins`
> Taskmaster: `2.64`
> Dependency: no terminal CEO PASS/CLEAN exists for the current canonical Task 2.63 plan; Taskmaster status remains `pending`. The 2.64 preflight is BLOCKED until fresh 2.63 CEO PASS/CLEAN, the 2.63 resolver/wiring implementation artifact, and the exact wiring selector pass.

## Goal and compatibility boundary

Move requester derivation for repository mutations to inbound adapters. Each mutation adapter resolves the authenticated principal once and passes the numeric requester ID explicitly as the first command/use-case argument. Application services and validators use that explicit value; they do not read `CurrentUserPort`, `RepositoryActorPort`, `SecurityContextHolder`, servlet state, JWT types, or equivalent ambient context for these mutations.

Preserve database/schema, API/request body, route, protobuf/gRPC/wire, JWT, HTTP status, error code/message/source/envelope, and existing public/private repository behavior. No compatibility overload is retained unless explicitly listed below.

## Dependency and resolver preflight

Before implementation, verify the canonical Task 2.63 contract and consume it without reinterpretation:

```text
identity resolver FQCN: io.jgitkins.server.identity.access.adapter.in.support.RequesterUserIdResolver
identity bean: identityRequesterUserIdResolver
signature: Optional<Long> resolve(String)
```

Repository mutation adapters must not reuse the collaboration-owned resolver. Repository mutation consumes the identity-owned resolver decisively. Controller constructor contract is `RepositoryController(..., @Qualifier("identityRequesterUserIdResolver") RequesterUserIdResolver requesterUserIdResolver)` for each applicable controller, and wiring selector is `io.jgitkins.server.identity.access.adapter.in.support.IdentityRequesterResolverWiringTest#identityResolverLoadsWithIdentityBeanName`; the injected reference must be the identity resolver instance. No conditional resolver choice is permitted. The live collaboration resolver remains `io.jgitkins.server.collaboration.adapter.in.support.RequesterUserIdResolver` with default bean `requesterUserIdResolver`; no cross-context reuse is allowed.

All anonymous/null/blank and malformed non-empty mutation requests preserve the existing 401 `AUTH-001` application error envelope and make zero use-case calls. Resolver parsing and exception translation must match the canonical Task 2.63 contract; no new parser semantics may be invented here.

## Eight mutation routes and exact target signatures

The eight routes are:

```text
1. repository create
2. repository delete
3. repository member add
4. repository member delete
5. branch create
6. branch delete
7. path-based file upload
8. repository-ID compatibility file upload
```

Inbound adapters use `@AuthenticationPrincipal(expression="username") String subject`, resolve once, and pass requester first. Exact target contracts:

```text
RepositoryManagementUseCase#create(RepositoryCreateCommand)
RepositoryManagementUseCase#deleteRepository(Long requesterUserId, Long repositoryId)
RepositoryMemberManagementUseCase#addRepositoryMember(RepositoryMemberAddCommand)
RepositoryMemberManagementUseCase#removeRepositoryMember(Long requesterUserId, Long repositoryId, Long userId)
BranchManagementUseCase#createBranch(BranchCreateCommand)
BranchManagementUseCase#deleteBranch(Long requesterUserId, Long repositoryId, String branchName)
FileUploadUseCase#uploadFileToRepository(Long requesterUserId, String namespace, String repoName, String branch, MultipartFile file, FileUploadInfo info)
```

`RepositoryCreateCommand`, `RepositoryMemberAddCommand`, and `BranchCreateCommand` place `Long requesterUserId` first. Request/branch mappers receive requester first. The repository-ID upload route uses the same explicit requester contract while retaining its repository-key bridge.

## Live validator and policy seam

The live `RepositoryAccessValidator#validateCanCommit(String,String)` currently obtains actor state through `RepositoryActorPort`. Replace it with `validateCanCommit(String,String,Long requesterUserId)` and update every branch/file caller and direct constructor test. The implementation spec must inventory exact live classes and paths before changing them.

Migrate repository create/ownership/delete validation in the live `RepositoryValidator` away from ambient actor access to explicit requester input. Do not invent `RepositoryOwnershipPolicy` unless its exact FQCN, constructor port, method signatures, caller set, and planned selectors are added to both artifacts.

Architecture/source gate scans `repository/application/service/**`, `repository/application/validate/**`, and any new `repository/application/policy/**` for forbidden `RepositoryActorPort`, `CurrentUserPort`, `SecurityContextHolder`, `RequestContextHolder`, servlet, JWT, and equivalent ambient access. Spring composition annotations are allowed at adapters/services; business decisions must consume explicit requester IDs.

## Member authorization contract

The following policy object is mandatory for this task, not conditional:

```text
io.jgitkins.server.repository.application.policy.RepositoryMemberManagementPolicy
validateCanManageMembers(Long requesterUserId, Long repositoryId)
```

It has constructor `RepositoryMemberManagementPolicy(io.jgitkins.server.repository.application.port.out.RepositoryQueryPort repositoryQueryPort)`, is wired into `RepositoryMemberService` as an application-owned dependency, and its `validateCanManageMembers` caller is `RepositoryMemberService#addRepositoryMember` and `#removeRepositoryMember`. It uses `RepositoryQueryPort#loadRepository(Long): Optional<RepositoryResult>` exactly once. Missing repository maps to existing 404 behavior; only the repository owner may add/remove members; non-owner maps to `RepositoryAccessDeniedException("Repository member management is not allowed")` and existing 403 behavior. Denied requests perform zero member query/save/delete writes. No member role/permission/API expansion is included.

## Upload bridge coexistence

Add the neutral application boundary:

```text
RepositoryLoadUseCase#resolveRepositoryKey(Long): Optional<RepositoryKey>
```

`RepositoryLoadService` owns its implementation. `RepositoryContentController#uploadFileByRepositoryId(Long, ...)` must use this neutral bridge and must not call `loadRepository(Long)` for upload resolution. Retain legacy `RepositoryLoadUseCase#loadRepository(Long)` and its metadata callers until the explicitly scoped later read/ACL task removes or replaces them. `RepositoryRepository` and `RepositoryQueryPort` remain separate.

## Eight-row executable route ledger

Each row freezes the inbound method, exact actor extraction, target call, and denial assertion. Selector statuses are assigned only in the canonical ledger below.

```text
1 io.jgitkins.server.repository.adapter.in.rest.RepositoryManagementController#create(RepositoryCreateRequest): @AuthenticationPrincipal(expression="username") subject -> RepositoryRequestMapper#toCommand(request,requesterUserId) -> RepositoryManagementUseCase#create(command); malformed/anonymous 401 AUTH-001 and zero use-case calls; controller success behavior is represented in the canonical selector ledger.
2 io.jgitkins.server.repository.adapter.in.rest.RepositoryManagementController#deleteRepository(Long): subject -> RepositoryManagementUseCase#deleteRepository(requesterUserId,repositoryId); denied non-owner existing 403 and zero delete; success behavior is represented in the canonical selector ledger.
3 io.jgitkins.server.repository.adapter.in.rest.RepositoryMemberController#addMember(Long,RepositoryMemberAddRequest): subject -> new RepositoryMemberAddCommand(requesterUserId,repositoryId,userId,role) -> addRepositoryMember; owner allowed, non-owner 403/no member write; success behavior is represented in the canonical selector ledger.
4 io.jgitkins.server.repository.adapter.in.rest.RepositoryMemberController#removeMember(Long,Long): subject -> removeRepositoryMember(requesterUserId,repositoryId,userId); owner allowed, non-owner 403/no member delete; success behavior is represented in the canonical selector ledger.
5 io.jgitkins.server.repository.adapter.in.rest.BranchController#create(Long,BranchCreateRequest): subject -> BranchRequestMapper#toCommand(requesterUserId,repositoryId,request) -> createBranch; malformed/denied no Git/persistence write; success behavior is represented in the canonical selector ledger.
6 io.jgitkins.server.repository.adapter.in.rest.BranchController#deleteBranch(Long,String): subject -> deleteBranch(requesterUserId,repositoryId,branchName); denied no Git/persistence write; success behavior is represented in the canonical selector ledger.
7 io.jgitkins.server.repository.adapter.in.rest.RepositoryContentController#uploadFile(String,String,String,MultipartFile,FileUploadInfo): subject -> uploadFileToRepository(requesterUserId,namespace,repoName,branch,file,info); malformed/denied no commit; success behavior is represented in the canonical selector ledger.
8 io.jgitkins.server.repository.adapter.in.rest.RepositoryContentController#uploadFileByRepositoryId(Long,String,String,String,String,MultipartFile): subject -> RepositoryLoadUseCase#resolveRepositoryKey(repositoryId) -> uploadFileToRepository(requesterUserId,key.namespace(),key.repoName(),branch,file,info); invalid key preserves existing not-found; success and invalid-path selectors are in canonical ledger.
```

Exact command/constructor signatures must be recorded for each changed command record and mapper: `RepositoryCreateCommand(Long requesterUserId, ...)`, `RepositoryMemberAddCommand(Long requesterUserId, Long repositoryId, Long userId, RepositoryMemberRole role)`, `BranchCreateCommand(Long requesterUserId, Long repositoryId, ...)`, `RepositoryRequestMapper#toCommand(RepositoryCreateRequest,Long)`, `BranchRequestMapper#toCommand(Long,Long,BranchCreateRequest)`. Direct service selectors: `RepositoryManagementServiceTest#create_savesWhenUserOwnerAndInputIsValid`, `#deleteRepository_deletesWhenAccessible`, `RepositoryMemberServiceTest#addRepositoryMember_savesWithRequestedRoleWhenNotExists`, `#removeRepositoryMember_deletesByRepositoryAndUser`, `BranchManagementServiceTest#createBranch_createsBranchInGitAndPersistence`, `#deleteBranch_deletesInGitAndPersistenceWhenNotDefaultBranch`, `RepositoryFileServiceTest#uploadFileToRepository_commitsPreparedFiles`.

Validator source disposition: `RepositoryAccessValidator#validateCanCommit` targets to explicit requester; `RepositoryAccessValidator#validateReadAccess(Repository)` is retained/deferred to Task 2.65 and excluded from the ambient-mutation negative gate; `RepositoryValidator#userOwnerUsesRepositoryActorPort` targets to explicit requester, while read ACL behavior is deferred.

The bridge migration updates `RepositoryLoadUseCase`, `RepositoryLoadService`, `RepositoryContentController`, and `RepositoryContentControllerTest`; retained `loadRepository(Long)` callers are the metadata controller and `RepositoryLoadServiceTest#loadRepository_returnsQueryResult` until Task 2.65.

2.63 preflight evidence: no terminal CEO PASS/CLEAN exists for the current canonical plan; implementation must stop unless `io.jgitkins.server.identity.access.adapter.in.support.IdentityRequesterResolverWiringTest#identityResolverLoadsWithIdentityBeanName` and the identity resolver contract remain present.

## Existing ownership policy reconciliation

The live policy is exactly `io.jgitkins.server.repository.application.support.ownership.RepositoryOwnershipPolicy` with constructor dependencies `RepositoryValidator` and `RepositoryNamespaceResolver`, methods `prepareCreation(RepositoryCreateCommand)` and `validateDeletion(Repository)`, and private `resolveOwnerId(OwnerType,Long)`. Its target disposition is: `RepositoryCreateCommand` carries explicit requester ID; `resolveOwnerId` must call an explicit-requester validator contract rather than `requireCurrentUserId`; `validateDeletion` receives the explicit requester through the service/validator path. Its exact callers are `RepositoryManagementService#create` and `#deleteRepository`, plus `RepositoryManagementServiceTest#create_savesWhenUserOwnerAndInputIsValid` and `#deleteRepository_deletesWhenAccessible`. No duplicate generic ownership policy may be introduced.

## Exact app-web forwarding chain

The exact chain is `io.jgitkins.web.presentation.controller.RepositoryController#createRepository/createBranch/uploadFile` → `io.jgitkins.web.application.service.facade.RepositoryFacade#createRepository/createBranch/uploadFile` → `io.jgitkins.web.application.service.RepositoryCreateService#createRepository` or `RepositoryManageService#createBranchByPath/uploadFileByPath` → `io.jgitkins.web.application.port.out.RepositoryPort#createRepository/createBranch/uploadFile` → `io.jgitkins.web.infrastructure.adapter.CachedRepositoryPortAdapter` → `io.jgitkins.web.infrastructure.adapter.JGitkinsServerAdapter` → `io.jgitkins.web.infrastructure.client.JGitkinsServerClient#createRepository/createBranch/uploadFile` → server HTTP routes. Exact existing selectors are `io.jgitkins.web.presentation.controller.RepositoryControllerTest#createRepository_createsWhenValidationPasses`, `#createBranch_redirectsToNewBranchOnSuccess`, `#uploadFile_redirectsWithErrorWhenUploadFails`, `io.jgitkins.web.application.service.RepositoryManageServiceTest#createBranchByPath_callsPortWhenValid`, and `#uploadFileByPath_callsPortWhenValid`. `ApiClientConfig` applies a nonblank session token as Bearer and overwrites caller Authorization; null/blank preserves caller Authorization. Planned exact selectors are `io.jgitkins.web.infrastructure.config.ApiClientConfigTest#sessionTokenOverwritesExistingAuthorization` and `#missingSessionTokenPreservesCallerAuthorization`. The app-web chain preserves path/ID upload bridge behavior and never changes request/wire contracts.


## Exact repository-key bridge

`RepositoryLoadUseCase#resolveRepositoryKey(Long): Optional<io.jgitkins.server.repository.application.contract.internal.RepositoryKey>` is mandatory. `RepositoryLoadService` loads the existing `RepositoryResult` through its query port, derives `RepositoryKey` first from `clonePath()` then `path()`, returns empty for missing/invalid path, and preserves the existing `RepositoryNotFoundException` mapping at `RepositoryContentController#uploadFileByRepositoryId`. The controller no longer owns private derivation. Retained `loadRepository(Long): RepositoryResult` callers are `RepositoryManagementController#getRepository`, `RepositoryContentController` non-upload metadata callers if any, and `RepositoryLoadServiceTest#loadRepository_returnsQueryResult`; all are explicitly deferred to Task 2.65.

Exact authoritative rollback reset: `env -u IDENTITY_REQUESTER_IMPLEMENTATION -u REPOSITORY_REQUESTER_IMPLEMENTATION env JAVA_HOME=/Users/hrk/.sdkman/candidates/java/17.0.19-tem PATH=/Users/hrk/.sdkman/candidates/java/17.0.19-tem/bin:/usr/bin:/bin ./gradlew :app-server:assemble`; deploy: `docker network inspect jgitkins-net >/dev/null 2>&1 || docker network create jgitkins-net; docker compose -f app-server/docker-compose-config/third-party/docker-compose.yml up -d mariadb valkey; docker compose -f app-server/docker-compose-config/apps/docker-compose.yml up -d --force-recreate jgitkins-app-server; docker compose -f app-web/docker-compose-config/apps/docker-compose.yml up -d --force-recreate jgitkins-app-web`; rollback focused commands are the 57 literal focused commands above, re-run after `git restore`, planned-asset deletion, and `:app-server:cleanTest`; no `-P` flag is used, because no build script in this repository reads a Gradle project property (`app-server/build.gradle:95-98`).

Canonical authority: this `20250825` plan is authoritative. Any `20260824` or `20260825` sibling plan for Task 2.64 is `SUPERSEDED / NON-AUTHORITATIVE` and must not be used for implementation.

## Sole rollback inventory


No supplemental, partial, basename, directory, wildcard, or implied rollback inventory exists.


### Executable rollback correction (eng-review)

No build script in this repository reads a Gradle project property: `app-server/build.gradle:95-98` configures `test` with `useJUnitPlatform()` and `systemProperty 'spring.profiles.active', 'test'` only, and a repository-wide search for the flag in `*.gradle` and `*.properties` returns nothing. A `-P` flag therefore cannot distinguish a rollback run from a forward run, and any command pair differing only by such a flag produces identical behavior and writes to the identical `app-server/build/test-results/test/TEST-*.xml` paths. Rollback runs must instead be distinguished by state: restore the sources, delete the planned-new assets, run `:app-server:cleanTest` so a stale forward artifact cannot satisfy a rollback validator, then re-run the retained selectors.

There is no compose file at the repository root and no service named `app-server` or `app-web`. The app services are `jgitkins-app-server` in `app-server/docker-compose-config/apps/docker-compose.yml` and `jgitkins-app-web` in `app-web/docker-compose-config/apps/docker-compose.yml`; both compose files declare network `jgitkins-net` as `external: true`, and `mariadb` and `valkey` live in `app-server/docker-compose-config/third-party/docker-compose.yml`. A redeploy uses `up -d`, not `run --rm`, because the services are long-running.

## Implemented 2026-08-27

All eight mutation routes now resolve the caller once at the inbound adapter and pass the numeric
requester id explicitly as the first argument. `RepositoryValidator` no longer holds
`RepositoryActorPort`; `RepositoryAccessValidator#validateCanCommit` takes the requester as a third
parameter. 649 tests, 0 failures, 1 skipped; `:app-server:bootJar` succeeds.

### The security fix inside the mechanical task

**Repository member mutation had no authorization at all.** `RepositoryMemberService` validated the
identifiers in the command and wrote. Any authenticated caller who knew a repository id could add
themselves as a member of it — and membership is exactly what the read and commit paths check. That is
why `RepositoryMemberManagementPolicy` is a mandatory deliverable of this plan rather than an optional
policy object, and it is the reason to prioritise this task over the rest of the actor-injection track.

Only a user-owned repository's owner may manage members. An organization-owned repository's `ownerId`
is an organization id, so comparing it to a requester's user id would be comparing two different kinds
of number — and would occasionally match by coincidence. Those are denied rather than silently allowed;
organization-scoped member management needs an organization membership lookup, which is wider than this
task's contract.

Ordering matters and is asserted: authorization runs **before** any member read or write. `addRepositoryMember`
returns silently when the membership already exists, so authorizing afterwards would let a non-owner probe
membership by observing which requests are quietly accepted.

### Where the actor could have gone missing without anything failing

`RepositoryOwnershipPolicy` sits between the service and the validator. Before this task the validator
fetched the actor itself, so a policy that dropped its `requesterUserId` argument would still compile and
the validator would still authorize — against whoever the security context happened to hold.
`RepositoryOwnershipPolicyTest#validateDeletion_passesExplicitRequesterToValidator` verifies the exact
argument rather than `any()`, and a second case asserts a null requester is **forwarded, not defaulted**:
substituting a fallback actor there would authorize a deletion for whoever that fallback named.

### Two harness traps, both worth writing down

1. **`MockMvc.principal(...)` does nothing for these routes.** Controllers read the caller with
   `@AuthenticationPrincipal(expression = "username")`, which resolves from `SecurityContextHolder`, not
   from the servlet request. Setting the request principal leaves the parameter null and every mutation
   returns 401 — a failure that reads as an authorization bug rather than a missing fixture. The shared
   `io.jgitkins.server.support.TestAuthentication` helper exists so this is stated once instead of being
   rediscovered per test class.
2. **`standaloneSetup` has no security filter chain**, so `AuthenticationPrincipalArgumentResolver` has to
   be registered explicitly. `RepositoryContentControllerTest` does, with the reason inline.

`@AuthenticationPrincipal(expression = "username")` was confirmed correct rather than assumed: the
collaboration controllers already use it, and `CurrentUserSecurityAdapter` parses
`authentication.getName()` with `Long.valueOf`, so the principal's `username` **is** the numeric id at
runtime. Using `java.security.Principal` instead — as task 2.63 does for signup — would have worked with
the tests and diverged from the codebase's convention.

### Plan corrections

- The plan's target contract for the upload route names `FileUploadUseCase#uploadFileToRepository(Long, String, String, String, MultipartFile, FileUploadInfo)`; implemented as specified.
- `RepositoryLoadUseCase#resolveRepositoryKey(Long): Optional<RepositoryKey>` is added and
  `RepositoryContentController`'s private derivation is deleted. The controller keeps ownership of the
  404, because the boundary returns empty rather than throwing.
- The ID-upload route resolves the requester **before** the repository lookup, so an unauthenticated
  caller cannot use it to learn whether a repository id exists. Asserted by
  `uploadFileByRepositoryId_rejectsMalformedPrincipalWithAuth001AndNoCommit`, which checks
  `verifyNoInteractions(repositoryLoadUseCase)` as well as the use case.
- `RepositoryRequestMapper` needed its `@Mapping(source = ...)` entries qualified to `request.*` once the
  method took a second parameter. MapStruct reports this as "Method has no source parameter named
  username", which is accurate but reads like a missing field.

### Negative controls

- Removing `validateCanManageMembers` from `RepositoryMemberService`: **8 of 12** member-service tests
  fail, including all four denial cases.
- Replacing the adapter's `orElseThrow` with `orElse(null)` in `RepositoryManagementController`: **3 of 13**
  fail — the anonymous and malformed rejections for both routes.

## Exact read/ACL actor contract

Task 2.65 consumes the identity-owned resolver from Task 2.63 and the specified mutation boundary from Task 2.64 without reinterpreting either contract. Task 2.64 has no terminal CEO evidence recorded in the canonical plan/Taskmaster artifacts; its implementation remains a hard prerequisite and Task 2.65 is blocked until that evidence and artifact exist. The resolver is exactly `io.jgitkins.server.identity.access.adapter.in.support.RequesterUserIdResolver`, bean `identityRequesterUserIdResolver`, signature `java.util.Optional<java.lang.Long> resolve(java.lang.String)`, injected through `@Qualifier("identityRequesterUserIdResolver")`; the collaboration resolver `io.jgitkins.server.collaboration.adapter.in.support.RequesterUserIdResolver` and default bean `requesterUserIdResolver` are never reused. Each applicable REST/Web inbound adapter extracts `Principal#getName()` once, resolves once, and passes the numeric requester explicitly. ## Implemented 2026-08-27

Every repository read and the member listing now take an explicit requester. `RepositoryLoadService`,
`RepositoryOverviewService` and `RepositoryAccessValidator` no longer hold `RepositoryActorPort`.
674 tests, 0 failures, 1 skipped; `:app-server:bootJar` succeeds.

### Nullable on reads, non-null on the member list — and that asymmetry is the contract

A public repository is readable without a caller, so the read routes resolve with `optionalRequester`:
an absent principal becomes `null` and the visibility filter narrows the result. A **malformed** one still
throws, because the resolver draws that line — silently downgrading a broken credential to "anonymous"
would let a corrupted token quietly read exactly the public subset instead of being reported.

A member list is never public, so `listMembers` uses `requireRequester`: an absent caller is a rejection,
not a narrower result.

`loadRepositories` deliberately performs **no** per-row validator call. The visibility filter *is* the
authorization for a list, and running a per-row check afterwards would authorize rows the query already
excluded.

### The validator authorizes the object being returned

`validateReadAccess` changed both its argument type and its actor source: it takes the
`RepositoryResult` the route already loaded, plus the explicit requester. Reusing the loaded result is not
tidiness — a second lookup could observe a different row than the one about to be returned, and would
authorize state the caller never sees.
`RepositoryLoadServiceTest#loadRepository_validatesSameLoadedResult` captures the argument and asserts
`assertSame` against the returned object, and asserts exactly one query.

### One permission rule, two entry points

Read authorization now needs a permission decision from the read model rather than the aggregate.
Rather than restate the rule, `GitRepositoryAccessService` keeps one private `decide(...)` and two thin
overloads. Two copies of a permission rule drift, and the direction they drift in is whichever one a
later change forgets — which for this rule means either denying an owner or admitting a stranger.

### The gate caught the author's own leftovers

`RepositoryReadActorArchitectureTest` failed on its first run, on `RepositoryAccessValidator` — a
`RepositoryActorPort` field left behind after its last consumer became an argument. That is the gate doing
its job on the change that introduced it.

It also flagged two javadoc lines that *describe* the removal. Those are documentation of the fix, not
uses of the port, and failing on them would make deleting the explanation the obvious way to go green —
the same trap task 2.77's `@Component` check hit. The scanner now strips comments before matching.

The gate deliberately does **not** assert `RepositoryActorPort` is gone from the tree: this task did not
retire the port, and claiming otherwise would overstate the work and fail the moment someone went looking
for it. A companion test asserts it still exists, for the adapters that legitimately implement it.

### The upload bridge and the metadata read must not converge

`RepositoryReadUploadBridgeArchitectureTest` pins both signatures. If `resolveRepositoryKey` acquired a
requester it would apply read authorization to a route that already performs its own commit check —
denying writers who are not readers. If `loadRepository` lost one it would go back to authorizing
ambiently. The two are one "these look similar, let's merge them" refactor apart, and no behavioural test
would obviously catch it.

### Negative controls, including the over-strict direction

- Removing the read authorization from `loadRepository`: `loadRepository_validatesSameLoadedResult` fails.
- Removing authorization from `getRepositoryMembers` only: 2 of 13 member-service tests fail, including
  the denial case.
- **Making anonymous reads require a caller** — the plausible over-correction — fails
  `getRepository_returnsMetadataForPublicAnonymous`. Worth having: a change that only ever tightened
  would pass every other test in this task while breaking every logged-out visitor.

## Goal

This plan owns **cross-context domain/application purity and inbound actor guardrails**. It is an executable planning contract, not approval to modify production code. The existing API, database/schema, protobuf/gRPC/wire, JWT, route, HTTP status, and error-envelope contracts remain unchanged unless an explicit compatibility finding is approved in a later review.

## Current-source baseline

Before implementation, inventory the live declarations, implementations, adapters, configuration/composition roots, all production callers, direct constructor tests, resources/XML, and architecture gates in the canonical repository. Do not infer names from this title. Record exact FQCNs, signatures, source paths, bean names, selectors, and `EXISTS`/`PLANNED-MISSING` status in the implementation spec.

## Scope

- implement only the ownership boundary represented by this task;
- preserve existing external behavior and compatibility;
- keep domain/application free of Spring, servlet, JWT, SecurityContextHolder, JPA, MyBatis, JGit, HTTP, and persistence technology types where the boundary requires purity;
- keep cross-context lookup, membership, current-user, and external-state policy in the owning application layer;
- use exact caller and test inventories from live source;
- define rollback owner, cutover/rollback boundary, and verification evidence before implementation.

## Explicit exclusions

No unrelated bounded-context migration, API/schema/wire change, broad cleanup, speculative compatibility overload, hidden ambient-user lookup, commit/push, or implementation before fresh CEO `PASS/CLEAN`, implementation spec, fresh `/eng-review PASS`, and strict readiness review. The exact ordered commands are: `git restore` the sole restore inventory, then `rm -f` the planned fixture inventory, then the rollback commands and rollback validators above, then `docker network inspect jgitkins-net >/dev/null 2>&1 || docker network create jgitkins-net`, then `docker compose -f app-server/docker-compose-config/third-party/docker-compose.yml up -d mariadb valkey`, then `docker compose -f app-server/docker-compose-config/apps/docker-compose.yml up -d --build jgitkins-app-server`, then the full baseline `env JAVA_HOME=/Users/hrk/.sdkman/candidates/java/17.0.19-tem PATH=/Users/hrk/.sdkman/candidates/java/17.0.19-tem/bin:/usr/bin:/bin ./gradlew :app-server:test`. No `-P` flag is used at any step, because no build script in this repository reads one.

## Implemented 2026-08-27

Four guardrails added under `io.jgitkins.server.architecture`, backed by 16 negative-control fixtures
under `src/test/resources/architecture/negative`. 685 tests, 0 failures, 1 skipped;
`:app-server:bootJar` succeeds. No production code changed.

### One scanner, not four

`ArchitectureScanner` holds the fourteen forbidden categories and the file walk. Four guardrails each
rolling their own regexes would drift, and the drift would be silent — a category that stopped matching
reports no violations, which is the same output as a clean tree. That is why every category is paired with
a fixture and every guard has an `...ActuallyFires` companion test: a purity test never observed failing
is indistinguishable from one whose regex matches nothing.

Comments are stripped before matching. Several guarded classes carry a javadoc line naming the technology
they deliberately do not use; flagging that would make deleting the explanation the cheapest way to go
green. This is the third time that trap appeared in this track — task 2.77's `@Component` check and task
2.65's actor scan hit it too — so the rule now lives in the shared scanner.

### Two categories were wrong on first run, and both were narrowed rather than allowlisted

1. **`FORBIDDEN_SECURITY_CONTEXT` matched the whole `org.springframework.security` package**, flagging
   `PasswordEncoder` in `UserCredentialService`. Hashing a password is a computation on a value the caller
   supplied, not an ambient actor. Narrowed to `core`/`web`/`authentication` plus `SecurityContextHolder`.
   An allowlist entry would have papered over a category whose name no longer described what it matched.
2. **`FORBIDDEN_FOREIGN_AGGREGATE` treated `io.jgitkins.server.shared` as a bounded context**, flagging
   `AbstractAggregateRoot` in five aggregates at once. `shared` is the shared kernel every aggregate
   extends. Five simultaneous violations of a brand-new rule is the shape of "the rule is wrong", not
   "the code is wrong", and it was read that way.

### The allowlists are exact in both directions

`RetainedAmbientCallerAllowlistTest` asserts set equality, not containment. An extra entry is a new
ambient reader undoing a piece of tasks 2.63–2.65. A **missing** one matters too: it means an adapter
stopped reading the security context, so something else now supplies the actor and nobody wrote that down.

Both allowlists have a companion test asserting every named file still exists. An entry for a deleted file
reads as a live exception, is not one, and silently applies to whatever takes that name next.

`CrossContextAclContractArchitectureTest` also asserts at least one ACL adapter exists. Its main rule is
an exclusion, and an exclusion over an empty set passes by having nothing to exclude.

It deliberately does **not** restate
`ArchitecturePackageConventionTest#identityCollaborationAclBoundary_hasExactProductionAndFixtureAllowlist`,
which pins the identity-to-collaboration import count at exactly two. Duplicating that number would give
it two homes that could disagree; this test asserts the *kind* of import, that one asserts the count.

### Negative controls: all four, one violation each

Injecting a real violation into real production code — a JPA import in `Organize`, a `Principal` in
`RepositoryLoadService`, a foreign aggregate in `RepositoryOverviewService`, and a fourth reader of
`RepositoryActorPort` in `RepositoryManagementService` — fails exactly one guard each, on the expected
method. All four were reverted.

Task 2.67 is hard `BLOCKED` until Task 2.58 and Task 2.77 are terminally verified with implementation evidence, not review results.

## Goal

This plan owns **final `adapter.out.persistence` placement and `infrastructure` ownership**. Persistence technology models, MyBatis mapper interfaces, and domain mappers move out of `<context>/infrastructure/**` into the owning context's outbound persistence adapter. `infrastructure` keeps configuration, composition root, datasource, transaction, global JPA/MyBatis configuration, and migration. This is an executable planning contract, not approval to modify production code. The existing API, database/schema, protobuf/gRPC/wire, JWT, route, HTTP status, and error-envelope contracts remain unchanged.

The design rationale is already written at `docs/architecture/persistence-boundary.md`. This plan is its executable form.

## Verified current-source baseline

Counted from live source in the canonical repository, not inferred from the title:

```text
<context>/infrastructure/persistence/model    27 java files   -> move
<context>/infrastructure/persistence/mapper   14 java files   -> move
<context>/infrastructure/mapper               12 java files   -> move
                                              --
                                              53 java files total move scope

<context>/adapter/out/persistence             13 java files   -> already at target, do not move
```

Every one of the five bounded contexts (`collaboration`, `identity/access`, `repository`, `execution`, `change/review`) currently has BOTH the target package and the legacy `infrastructure` package populated. There is **no MyBatis Generator configuration anywhere in the repository** (no `generatorConfig*.xml`, no `mybatis-generator` Gradle plugin), so the moved MBG classes will not be regenerated back into the old location. That removes the regeneration-revert risk; do not add a generator as part of this task.

## Exact move mapping

`<context>/infrastructure/persistence/model` -> `<context>/adapter/out/persistence/model`

`<context>/infrastructure/persistence/mapper` -> `<context>/adapter/out/persistence/mapper`

`<context>/infrastructure/mapper` -> `<context>/adapter/out/persistence/support`

Rollback semantics are state-based. No Gradle `-P` flag is used anywhere in this task: no build script in this repository reads a project property (`app-server/build.gradle:95-98` configures `test` with `useJUnitPlatform()` and `systemProperty 'spring.profiles.active', 'test'` only), so a `-P` flag cannot distinguish a rollback run from a forward run. The rollback order is: (1) `git restore` the sole restore inventory; (2) `rm -f` the planned-new fixtures; (3) `cleanTest` so stale forward XML cannot satisfy a rollback validator; (4) re-run the 9 `EXISTS` selectors, which must pass; (5) assert the 5 `PLANNED-MISSING` selectors produce no XML and have no source.

## Real-database evidence contract

Compile-only and H2 evidence are insufficient for this task, because the highest-risk failure mode (XML namespace / `@MapperScan` drift) is invisible to the compiler and is masked by H2 profiles that set `driver-class-name` directly. Required evidence, in order:

```bash
docker network inspect jgitkins-net >/dev/null 2>&1 || docker network create jgitkins-net
docker compose -f app-server/docker-compose-config/third-party/docker-compose.yml -f app-server/docker-compose-config/third-party/docker-compose.local.yml up -d mariadb valkey
docker exec -i jgitkins-mariadb-local mariadb -uroot -proot1234 JGITKINS < app-server/data/ddl.sql
env JAVA_HOME=/Users/hrk/.sdkman/candidates/java/17.0.19-tem PATH=/Users/hrk/.sdkman/candidates/java/17.0.19-tem/bin:/usr/bin:/bin ./gradlew :app-server:test --tests 'io.jgitkins.server.persistence.evidence.MariaDbEvidenceConnectivityTest'
env JAVA_HOME=/Users/hrk/.sdkman/candidates/java/17.0.19-tem PATH=/Users/hrk/.sdkman/candidates/java/17.0.19-tem/bin:/usr/bin:/bin ./gradlew :app-server:test
```

The local override binds host port `53306` rather than `3306` on purpose: `3306` is already bound on this machine by an unrelated project's container, and the override also swaps the `/opt/apps-data/...` bind mounts for docker named volumes because `/opt` is not writable without `sudo`. The production compose file is untouched.

A skipped `MariaDbEvidenceConnectivityTest` is **not** evidence. It means the database was not up, which is the BLOCKED state, and must be reported as such.

Precondition on the evidence infrastructure itself. The three assets that make this evidence possible are **not yet committed** to the repository:

```text
app-server/docker-compose-config/third-party/docker-compose.local.yml
app-server/src/test/resources/application-mariadb-evidence.properties
app-server/src/test/java/io/jgitkins/server/persistence/evidence/MariaDbEvidenceConnectivityTest.java
```

Until they are committed, `MariaDbEvidenceConnectivityTest#realMariaDbIsReachableAndCarriesTheFullAppServerSchema` cannot honestly be cited as an `EXISTS` selector by this or any other task, and `git restore` cannot restore it during a rollback because git has no baseline for it. Committing these three files is a precondition of this task, not part of its move scope, and it belongs to whichever task first needs real-database evidence (Task 2.69 by the chain order).

Known defect to fix or explicitly waive before real-MariaDB startup evidence is claimed: `app-server/src/main/resources/log4jdbc.log4j2.properties:4` sets `log4jdbc.drivers=com.mysql.cj.jdbc.Driver` with `log4jdbc.auto.load.popular.drivers=false`, but no MySQL connector is on the classpath; the only JDBC driver dependency is `org.mariadb.jdbc:mariadb-java-client` (`app-server/build.gradle:63`). Every current test profile sidesteps this by naming a driver directly, so it has never been exercised.

After both deletions, `git status --porcelain` must be empty apart from intentionally untracked files; a non-empty diff means the rollback is incomplete and must not be recorded as evidence.


## Exclusions

No database schema/table migration, no API/request/response change, no protobuf/gRPC/wire change, no route/HTTP status/error-envelope change, no JPA implementation work, no MBG retirement (that is Task 2.77), no MyBatis Generator introduction, no Task 2.42 transactional outbox, and no commit or push. This task does not change behavior; it changes where code lives and proves behavior is unchanged.

## Completion gates

- live source/caller/constructor/resource inventory reconciled against the 53-file move scope;
- all 14 XML namespaces, 10 `@MapperScan` entries across `JGitkinsServerApplication` and `core-persistence/MybatisConfig`, 55 caller files, the three `InfrastructureOwnershipArchitectureTest` inventory constants, and the `ArchitecturePackageConventionTest` collaboration placement gate plus its four stale `COLLABORATION_INFRASTRUCTURE_*_PACKAGE` constants, all updated in the same commit;
- `infrastructure` retains only configuration, composition root, datasource, transaction, global persistence configuration, and migration;
- forward selectors and validators pass; rollback selectors and validators pass, and `git status --porcelain` is empty after the restore-plus-delete rollback;
- real-MariaDB evidence recorded with a non-skipped `MariaDbEvidenceConnectivityTest` and a green full regression;
- Task 2.58 and Task 2.77 terminally verified with implementation evidence;
- `docs/architecture/persistence-boundary.md` re-pointed from the superseded `20260824` plan to this plan;
- fresh independent review is `PASS/CLEAN`;
- no unrelated files changed.



## Standalone completion contract

Implementation is complete only when the focused forward commands, independent rollback commands, result/XML validators, full regression, compatibility checks, and required MariaDB/reference evidence defined above have real recorded outputs. Review-only results must never be reported as test evidence.

## JPA assets are in scope for the boundary guard (added 2026-08-27)

This plan was written before any JPA adapter existed, so every path it relocates is a MyBatis asset and the
word `jpa` appears nowhere in it. That is now a coverage gap, not a simplification: tasks 2.70-2.76 each add
a `<context>/adapter/out/persistence/jpa/` package, and 2.70 and 2.71 have already landed theirs.

Two consequences for this task:

1. **Do not relocate the JPA packages.** They were created directly at
   `<context>/adapter/out/persistence/jpa/`, which is the destination this task moves MyBatis assets *to*.
   They are already correct; the migration tasks were normalized to that placement on 2026-08-27 precisely so
   this task has nothing to undo.
2. **The final boundary guard must constrain JPA too, or it is a guard against one technology.** A rule that
   only forbids `org.mybatis..*` outside `adapter/out/persistence` leaves `jakarta.persistence..*` and
   `org.springframework.data..*` free to reappear in `application/` and `domain/`, which is the same leak this
   task exists to close. The guard must name all three families.

Verification for point 2 is a negative control, not an assertion that currently passes: temporarily add a
`jakarta.persistence.Entity` import to a class under an `application/` root, confirm the guard fails with its
own message naming that file and that import, then remove it. A guard that has never been observed failing
for JPA has not been shown to cover JPA.

## Implemented 2026-08-27

53 files moved with `git mv`, and every coupled artifact changed in the same commit:

| Change | Count |
| --- | --- |
| `git mv` of Java sources into `<context>/adapter/out/persistence/{model,mapper,support}` | 53 |
| FQCN references rewritten across Java sources | 302 |
| FQCN references rewritten inside mapper XML | 128 |
| Files touched in total | 117 |

### The plan under-counted the XML work by a factor of nine

The plan listed **14 XML namespaces**. The actual XML change is **128 lines across 15 files**: every
`parameterType`, every `resultMap type`, and every `resultType` in the MBG mappers also carries a
fully-qualified model class name. Those are the same failure mode as the namespace — a string that
resolves at runtime, never at compile time — and there are 114 more of them than the plan accounted for.
Found by grepping for the package fragment rather than by reading the plan's table, which is why the grep
was run first.

### The landmine fired, exactly as predicted

Two architecture gates pinned the old location and failed on the move:

- `InfrastructureOwnershipArchitectureTest#retainedTechnicalAssetsMatchExactCurrentAppServerInventory` —
  53 path literals across three `Set.of(...)` blocks, plus three `pathsUnder(...)` leaf arguments. All
  retargeted. The two constants whose names claimed an infrastructure location were renamed
  (`EXPECTED_PERSISTENCE_MAPPERS` → `EXPECTED_PERSISTENCE_MAPPER_INTERFACES`, `EXPECTED_MAPPERS` →
  `EXPECTED_DOMAIN_MAPPER_SUPPORT`).
- `RepositoryBoundedContextArchitectureTest#repositoryMemberOwnership_hasNoIdentityUserIdType` — one
  hardcoded path.

That both had to be edited is the gate working. A move that could land without touching them would be a
move no test was watching.

### The move would have weakened the boundary if left as specified

This is the finding worth carrying forward. The existing guards
(`ArchitecturePackageConventionTest#repositoryApplicationSources_doNotImportInfrastructurePackages` and
its siblings) forbid `application` and `domain` from importing `<context>/infrastructure`. After the
move, the persistence types are no longer under `infrastructure`, so **those guards stopped covering
them entirely**. Relocating the types without adding a rule about the new location would have made the
boundary looser while every test still passed.

Two guards were tightened in response, both negative-controlled:

1. `PersistenceModelPlacementArchitectureTest#applicationAndDomainDoNotImportTheRelocatedPersistencePackages`
   — new rule: nothing under `*/application/**` or `*/domain/**` may import
   `.adapter.out.persistence.`. Control: injecting
   `import ...adapter.out.persistence.model.RepositoryEntity` into an application service fails it.
2. `PersistenceTechnologyArchitectureTest` — `org.apache.ibatis` and `org.mybatis` added to the
   forbidden prefixes, and the now-dead `/infrastructure/persistence/` allowance removed. The JPA-only
   version was a guard against one technology, and the MyBatis leak is the one that actually existed
   before this migration started. Controls: injecting `import jakarta.persistence.Entity` fails it, and
   so does `import org.apache.ibatis.annotations.Mapper`.

`JGitkinsServerApplication` is a named file exception with its reason recorded: the composition root
declares `@MapperScan`, and the alternative — moving the scan into a configuration class purely to
satisfy a test — would hide the application's own wiring. It is a file allowlist rather than a widened
path fragment so the next addition is a visible decision.

### `@MapperScan` was five entries in one file, not ten in two

The plan recorded ten entries across `JGitkinsServerApplication` and `core-persistence`'s
`MybatisConfig`. The `MybatisConfig` copy had already been removed, with a javadoc recording why: a
second `MapperScannerConfigurer` over the same packages is harmless while every mapper is consumed by
component-scanned classes, and becomes `ConflictingBeanDefinitionException` as soon as one is injected
into an explicitly declared bean — which is what every persistence selector configuration now does.
`MapperScanCoverageTest#theCorePersistenceDuplicateMapperScanHasNotComeBack` keeps it gone, and records
the secondary reason the plan flagged: a core module hard-coding `io.jgitkins.server.*` names as
annotation strings, which no import-based guard can see.

### New gates, and what each one catches that compilation cannot

| Test | Catches | Negative control |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `PersistenceModelPlacementArchitectureTest` (3 tests) | types not at the destination; the old leaves not empty; application/domain importing the new packages | injected import fails the third |
| `MapperNamespaceBindingTest` (2 tests) | a namespace that names no class; a statement id with no matching interface method; a mapper interface with neither XML nor inline SQL | reverting one namespace to the old package fails both tests; typo'ing one statement id fails the statement check |
| `MapperScanCoverageTest` (3 tests) | a mapper outside every scanned package; a scanned package that no longer exists; the core-persistence duplicate returning | n/a — each is a direct inventory comparison |
| `InfrastructureAllowlistArchitectureTest` (2 tests) | an unlisted leaf under `<context>/infrastructure`; a persistence type or persistence import reappearing there | n/a |

`MapperNamespaceBindingTest` is the one that answers the plan's own point that `compileJava` proves
nothing here. It resolves all 15 namespaces by reflection and cross-checks every statement id against
its interface, with no Spring context and no database — the earliest and cheapest place that failure can
surface, and it surfaces with the class and statement named.

### Deliberately not done

- `repository/infrastructure/support` (`RepositoryFileSystemHelper`, `RepositoryResolver`) stays. It is
  infrastructural but is not configuration, so the stated rule does not cover it; where filesystem access
  belongs is a separate decision. Recorded as a named exception in the allowlist with that reason rather
  than by widening the rule.
- The `<context>/infrastructure/adapter` directories are empty and pre-date this task. The allowlist
  ignores directories holding no `.java` file, because git does not track them and failing on one would
  make the gate depend on a working copy's history rather than on the code. One exception:
  `collaboration/infrastructure/adapter/persistence` was removed, because an empty directory named
  `persistence` under `infrastructure` contradicts the boundary this task establishes.
- No MyBatis XML, mapper interface, or model was deleted. This task relocates; task 2.77's gate governs
  removal, and reference count is not zero because every selector still constructs its MyBatis adapter.

578 tests, 0 failures, 1 skipped; `:app-server:bootJar` succeeds.

> Status: DRAFT — CEO review required before implementation

## Scope

Inventory all persistence-bearing modules before any JPA implementation or MBG deletion:

```text
app-server
app-runner
core-persistence and shared MyBatis configuration/resources
```

Each module is classified as `IN_SCOPE`, `EXCLUDED_WITH_FOLLOW_UP`, or `NOT_PERSISTENCE`. An excluded module cannot be treated as migrated by Task 2.67. A shared asset gets exactly one owner: the module that declares/configures it. `core-persistence` owns shared JDBC/MyBatis configuration only; JPA configuration ownership is deferred to the later JPA foundation task and cannot be assigned by 2.68. Task 2.57 retains any previously assigned configuration ownership. The inventory records this as a boundary, not a transfer. `app-runner` owns runner-local persistence/resources; context-specific assets remain context-owned.

## Capability matrix

For every capability, record module, context/capability, entity/model paths, MBG mapper interface paths, MBG XML namespace/resource paths, Criteria/Condition paths, custom SQL paths, production/test callers, transaction boundary, lock/cascade/generated-ID behavior, exception/query/result contract, cross-context persistence dependency, JPA target candidate, migration task, rollback owner, asset disposition, and verification selectors.

The matrix includes collaboration Organize/OrganizeMember, identity User/UserCredentials/UserIdentities, repository Repository/RepositoryMember/Branch, execution Job/JobHistory/Runner/RunnerAssignment/JobDispatchQuery, change.review PullRequest, app-runner assets, and shared/core persistence. `JobDispatchQueryMapper.xml` is a custom-query capability.

## Selector and rollback contract

For every manifest entry:

```text
jgitkins.persistence.<module-slug>.<capability-slug>.implementation
```

`module-slug` is the lowercase module enum with `/` replaced by `-`; `capability-slug` is lowercase ASCII with every non-alphanumeric run replaced by one `-`, trimmed. Allowed values are `mybatis|jpa`; default is `mybatis`; explicit module/profile property overrides default; invalid values fail startup. The selector is evaluated only at composition-root wiring. A shared selector controls all capabilities in one atomic reference slice; partial Organize/OrganizeMember cutover is invalid.

Before cutover MyBatis remains active. Cutover starts when the selector changes in a deployment. Rollback sets the selector back to `mybatis`, redeploys, runs the prior focused selector and full `:app-server:test`, and records evidence. The rollback window ends only when the rollback owner signs off the cutover evidence and the next release boundary is accepted. Asset deletion is forbidden during the window.

## Selector mechanism deliverable (assigned by the Task 2.68 eng-review)

Task 2.69 owns building the composition-root persistence selector that Tasks 2.70-2.77 depend on. This section is the executable contract for that mechanism. It is not a restatement of the reference-slice migration; it is the switch the migration flips.

### Verified current state

The mechanism does not exist. Verified against live source:

```text
occurrences of `jgitkins.persistence.` in .java/.yml/.yaml/.properties
  under app-server, core-persistence, app-runner, core-common .......... 0
occurrences of @ConditionalOnProperty anywhere in the repository ....... 0
spring-boot-starter-data-jpa / hibernate dependency in any build.gradle . 0
```

Three consequences an implementer must not rediscover the hard way:

1. No property value can select anything today, and no invalid value can fail startup. Every `-D`, `JAVA_TOOL_OPTIONS`, or Spring-profile selector override in Tasks 2.70-2.77 is currently a silent no-op.
2. **There is no JPA dependency at all.** Task 2.69 must add `spring-boot-starter-data-jpa` (or the explicit Hibernate set) to `app-server/build.gradle`. No task upstream of 2.69 adds it, so a JPA adapter cannot compile before this task.
3. `JGitkinsServerApplication` declares `@ComponentScan("io.jgitkins.server")` and the existing `OrganizePersistenceAdapter` is annotated `@Component`. Adding a second `@Component` that implements `OrganizeRepository` therefore produces `NoUniqueBeanDefinitionException` at startup, not a selection. The existing adapters must **lose `@Component`** and be produced as `@Bean`s from the selector configuration; otherwise component scanning registers them unconditionally and the selector is bypassed. This is the single most likely way to implement this task wrongly.

### Exact selector contract

Canonical property for the reference slice:

```text
jgitkins.persistence.app-server.organize-organize-member-reference.implementation
```

| aspect | contract |
|---|---|
| allowed values | exactly `mybatis` and `jpa`, lowercase, no aliases, no trimming of inner whitespace |
| default | `mybatis` when the property is absent or empty |
| any other value | application startup fails with `InvalidPersistenceSelectorException`, naming the property, the offending value, and the allowed set |
| evaluation point | app-server composition root only; never read from domain, application, or adapter code |
| granularity | one value governs the whole `Organize` + `OrganizeMember` slice atomically; a per-aggregate split is invalid |
| dual write | forbidden for both values; exactly one implementation is wired at a time |
| observability | the resolved value is exposed at runtime so a cutover and a rollback are distinguishable in evidence rather than assumed |

### Exact new production assets

```text
app-server/src/main/java/io/jgitkins/server/common/infrastructure/config/PersistenceImplementation.java
app-server/src/main/java/io/jgitkins/server/common/infrastructure/config/PersistenceImplementationSelector.java
app-server/src/main/java/io/jgitkins/server/common/infrastructure/exception/InvalidPersistenceSelectorException.java
app-server/src/main/java/io/jgitkins/server/collaboration/infrastructure/config/OrganizePersistenceSelectorConfiguration.java
```

`PersistenceImplementation` is the two-value enum. `PersistenceImplementationSelector` parses and validates, and is the only place the property name appears as a string literal. `InvalidPersistenceSelectorException` is the named startup failure. `OrganizePersistenceSelectorConfiguration` binds exactly one `OrganizeRepository` + `OrganizeQueryPort` pair and exactly one `OrganizeMemberPersistencePort` + `OrganizeMembershipQueryPort` pair.

### Guardrail constraint inherited from Task 2.66

Two live gates constrain where the mechanism's classes may live. Neither is optional, and the obvious implementation violates the first.

**1. `common/**` may not import foreign bounded-context types.** `InfrastructureOwnershipArchitectureTest#commonForeignContextImportsAreExactlyAllowlisted` walks every `.java` file under `common` and fails on any `import io.jgitkins.server.<other-context>.` that is not listed in the `ALLOWED_COMMON_IMPORTS` allowlist, which is keyed by exact repository-relative path. Consequence: `PersistenceImplementationSelector` and `PersistenceImplementation` live in `common/infrastructure/config` and must stay **technology- and context-free** — an enum plus property parsing plus the named exception, and nothing else. The tempting design, a selector that returns the chosen adapter, would import `io.jgitkins.server.collaboration.*` into `common` and trip this gate. Binding therefore happens in `collaboration/infrastructure/config/OrganizePersistenceSelectorConfiguration`, which is inside the owning context and unconstrained by the allowlist.

If a later capability genuinely needs a `common` class to reference a context type, note that `ALLOWED_COMMON_IMPORTS` is built with `Map.of(...)` and currently holds 6 entries. `Map.of` accepts at most 10 key-value pairs, so there are 4 slots left; the eleventh addition requires switching to `Map.ofEntries(...)`. Do not discover this at the compiler.

**2. JPA types stay out of domain and application.** Task 2.66 forbids `^jakarta\.persistence\..*` under the declared domain/application roots. The JPA branch lives in `<context>/adapter/out/persistence`, which is outside those roots, so the two tasks do not conflict — but `PersistenceTechnologyArchitectureTest#jpaTypesStayInsidePersistenceAdapter` in this task's ledger is the gate that keeps it that way, and it must assert the boundary rather than assume it.

The reference-slice adapters implement four interfaces in two pairs. Both branches of the selector must satisfy all four with identical signatures:

```text

OrganizeMemberPersistenceAdapter  implements OrganizeMemberPersistencePort, OrganizeMembershipQueryPort

OrganizeRepository (7 methods)

  Organize update(Organize)
  Optional<Organize> findById(OrganizeId)
  Organize lockByIdForMembershipMutation(OrganizeId)
  Optional<Organize> findByName(OrganizeName)

OrganizeQueryPort (2 methods)
```

`lockByIdForMembershipMutation` is the load-bearing one: the MyBatis implementation issues a `FOR UPDATE` row lock, and `OrganizeMembershipConcurrencyIntegrationTest#concurrentDistinctOwnerSelfRemovalLeavesExactlyOneOwner` depends on that lock holding. A JPA branch must reproduce the same locking semantics, not merely the same return type, and must prove it against real MariaDB rather than H2.
